name: Mid-South Wire Products Inc.
old_description: Since 1967, Mid-South Wire has been a proud, family-owned business delivering high-quality wire products to its customers. Based in the heart of Nashville, Tennessee, the company is widely respected as an industry leader known for its innovation and exceptional service.
about:
Mid-South Wire Products Inc. was founded in 1967 by John T. Johnson, Sr. in Nashville, Tennessee. The company remains family-owned, now led by John T. Johnson, Jr., and operates a second facility in Scott City, Missouri. Its origins trace to a single “sidewinder” bull-block drawing machine acquired in 1964, which still sits outside the Nashville offices as a reminder of the firm’s humble start.

The company manufactures carbon steel wire products including wire rod, bright basic wire, plating-quality wire, nitrogen-wiped galvanized wire (Class 1–4 per ASTM A-641), and welded wire mesh for concrete reinforcement. Production runs on more than 30 wire-drawing machines, supported by a modern pickle room, a high-speed Morgan Koch multi-pass drawing line, a galvanizing line, and an overhead railcar-unloading system. A dedicated tractor-trailer fleet and a private barge operation on the Cumberland River provide direct shipping options.

Mid-South Wire serves automotive seating suppliers such as Lear Seigler, Hoover Universal, and Johnson Controls, as well as cable manufacturer Copperweld and shelving producer Lee Rowan (later Rubbermaid). Its customer base spans the automotive, construction, cable, and industrial storage sectors throughout the Southeast and beyond.

The firm differentiates itself with a just-in-time delivery model built on in-stock inventory, company-owned trucks, and river barge access, promising on-time delivery for every order. Family values and a “can-do” culture—evident in the rapid recovery after the 1975 Cumberland River flood—underpin its commitment to service and continuous equipment investment.

name: Midian Electronics
old_description: Midian Electronics was founded in 1975 specializing in after-market 2805/1500 Hz and 600/1500 Hz MTS pulse tone decoders, SECODE SMART/IMTS/DTMF radio-telephone encoders-decoders with ANI. We specialized in
about:
Midian Electronics was founded in 1975 by Chuck Soulliard in Tucson, Arizona. The company began by specializing in after-market 2805/1500 Hz and 600/1500 Hz MTS pulse tone decoders, as well as SECODE SMART/IMTS/DTMF radio-telephone encoders-decoders with ANI. Its name derives from "Miniature Digital and Analog," reflecting the focus on compact electronic modules for land mobile radio.

Today Midian designs and manufactures a broad line of radio communication products, including tone signaling modules (DTMF, pulse tone, two-tone, five-tone), voice security devices such as voice scramblers and AES-128 bit encryption, tone remote desk sets, termination panels, two-way radio interoperability switches, remote control and monitoring systems, fleet management, telephone interconnects, paging and alarm products, and plug-in modules for OEM radios. The company also offers in-house custom electronic circuit design, PCB layout, and product development services. All products are designed and built at its Tucson facility and carry a three-year parts and labor warranty.

Midian's equipment serves public safety agencies (police, fire, ambulance), fleet operators (taxi, towing, fishing), government and military users, industrial and commercial businesses, and OEM radio manufacturers. Its interoperability solutions, for example, bridge LTE to VHF or connect Site Connect to P25 networks.

The company distinguishes itself by being the first to bring after-market MTS pulse tone decoders to market and by introducing the world's first voice scrambler small enough to fit inside a portable two-way radio. Midian states its mission is to continue providing innovative, after-market products that improve the safety and versatility of two-way radio networks.

about:
Midlands Packaging Corporation has operated from Lincoln, Nebraska since its founding on April 1, 1972. The company remains locally owned and managed, with sales offices across the Midwest in Dallas, Denver, Kansas City, Minneapolis, Omaha, St. Louis, and Sioux City.

The manufacturer produces folding cartons, corrugated containers, thermoformed plastics, laminated cartons, specialty boxes, and point-of-purchase displays. Structural design uses CAD linked to CAM, and the 170-person workforce averages 15 years of tenure.

Midlands serves retail and pharmaceutical customers requiring packaging that meets FDA regulations (21 CFR 176.180, 211.122) and Federal Specification PPP-B-566E, as well as food-industry clients covered by its SQF Level 1 certification. The quality system follows ANSI/ASQ Z1.4 sampling, and the plant holds FSC Chain of Custody certification.

The company emphasizes assigned account teams — each customer receives a dedicated sales person and service representative — and highlights its in-house die shop, long-tenured staff, and 100% recycling of production waste as operational differentiators.

name: Midwestern Wood Products Company
old_description: Coffered ceilings, in historic architecture, were created by arranging coffers (or framed boxes) in interesting configurations on a ceiling. The coffers were square, rectangular or octagonal and most often had deep recesses and were originally made out of stone. Eventually wood coffered ceilings replaced stone structures because a lighter weight material was more desirable.
about:
Midwestern Wood Products Company has operated from Peoria, Illinois since its founding in 1968. The company traces its expertise to the development of the WOODGRID® Suspended Coffered Ceiling System, a wood-based drop-ceiling solution designed to replicate historic coffered aesthetics with modern installation methods.

The company manufactures the WOODGRID® system, which consists of main runners, cross tees, and drop-in coffer panels that create depth and architectural interest. The panels are removable, allowing access to mechanical and electrical systems above the ceiling. Midwestern Wood Products offers multiple styles, wood species, and finishes, and coordinates with Heritage Restoration and Design for custom finishing techniques such as antique painting. The system accommodates various ceiling conditions including high, low, cathedral, and basement heights, and integrates with lighting, venting, soffits, and home theater components.

The product serves both residential and commercial markets. In homes, it is used in libraries, studies, dens, offices, and basements where access to ductwork is needed. Commercial applications include restaurants, lobbies, and other venues where a non-commercial, cozy appearance is desired. The company notes that the system is suitable for new construction and remodel projects alike.

Midwestern Wood Products emphasizes that its WOODGRID® ceiling is American-made, affordable, and installs similarly to a standard metal grid system. The company also highlights its 40 years of experience in decorative wood drop ceilings and its ability to customize layouts for each space.

old_description: Since 1963, Mighty has been the gold standard of parts distribution exclusively to the automotive service professional. Our trademark combination of high quality products, inventory management, superior personal service, and competitive pricing set us apart as the premier stocking supplier. In today's world when so-called customer service, support teams, and suppliers are often literally separated by oceans, it's good to know Mighty parts, service, technical support and business expertise you need are available from your local Mighty Representative.
about:
Mighty Auto Parts operates a wholesale distribution franchise in Henderson, Nevada. The Henderson location is managed by designated manager Scott Worrall and serves the local market with bilingual English and Spanish support.

The company distributes automotive replacement parts sourced from original-equipment manufacturers, carrying product lines that include brakes, filters, batteries, belts and tensioners, chemicals, hardware and fasteners, motor oil and lubricants, shop supplies, tire-service items, tools and equipment, wipers, and personal protection equipment. Beyond parts supply, the franchise provides value-added services such as professional inventory management, obsolescence protection, business consulting, customized technician training, an online catalog (MIC), a Rapid Rewards loyalty program, shop-management software, and marketing support.

Customers are exclusively professional automotive service providers — independent repair shops, dealership service departments, and fleet maintenance operations — in the Henderson area. The business model is strictly B2B wholesale; no retail or consumer sales are conducted at this location.

Mighty positions its differentiation on local accessibility and service depth: a dedicated representative is available on-site rather than through offshore call centers, and the combination of inventory management, technical support, and business expertise is intended to protect shop profitability against parts obsolescence and supply-chain gaps.

name: Mike's Metal Works
old_description: Founded by Mike Winters in 1986, we specialize in copper, zinc, lead and stainless steel. Three generations of knowledge, time tested tools and machinery and our traditional, small operation ensures the very best quality, materials and service that money can buy. This traditional approach to the techniques translates to the customer experience as well. Our small operation ensures an unmatched product and unrivaled customer satisfaction.
about:
Mike's Metal Works operates from Bozeman, Montana, where founder Mike Winters established the shop in 1986 after years in roofing and sheet metal. The business draws on three generations of metalworking knowledge; a shop anvil passed down from Winters' grandfather has been in the family for over a century.

The company produces custom architectural metalwork, specializing in copper, zinc, lead, and stainless steel roofing systems built with traditional techniques such as double-lock standing seam, flat seam, and soldered joints. A full-service fabrication shop houses shears, brakes, rolls, turners, punches, a forge, welders, plasma cutting, roll forming, and an English wheel, enabling production of cupolas, gutters, range hoods, and other custom pieces. Welding capabilities cover copper, steel, stainless steel, aluminum, and exotic alloys. The shop runs without computer-aided layout, relying on trammels, dividers, and rules, and employs only two or three workers to maintain personal oversight.

The firm's work has been featured in Cowboys and Indians magazine.

Winters emphasizes a traditional, small-scale approach as the differentiator: time-tested hand tools, multi-generational expertise, and a lean crew ensure quality and responsive service on each project.

old_description: Welcome to the Mill End Store! We are a family-owned fabric store located in Milwaukie, Oregon since 1918, and Beaverton, OR since the 1980s. about:
Mill End Store operates from two locations in the Portland metropolitan area: its original Milwaukie, Oregon site opened in 1918 and a Beaverton branch added in the 1980s. The business has remained family-owned throughout its history, beginning as one of the West Coast’s first worsted wool mills that supplied military uniforms during both world wars and provided yarn for early Jantzen knitted swimwear.

Today the company functions as a specialty fabric retailer with more than 50,000 square feet of combined retail space stocking designer runs, one-of-a-kind fabrics, trims, and notions. Inventory turns daily, and the store fulfills orders by phone and mail for customers worldwide, supplemented by a swatch service and special-order program.

The customer base spans professional costumers for film and television, nationally recognized fashion designers, interior designers, quilters, crafters, and novice sewists. Shoppers regularly travel from across the country to visit the physical stores, which are open Tuesday through Saturday.

The company emphasizes its century-long continuity, knowledgeable staff with sewing expertise, and a reputation for carrying hard-to-find materials that draws a global clientele despite the absence of an online store.

name: Minneapolis Sheet Metal Works
old_description: Minneapolis Sheet Metal Works was founded over a century ago in the heart of downtown Minneapolis. Our roots stem from working with the booming commodity industry by designing unique dust collection solutions for grain elevators and mills.
about:
Minneapolis Sheet Metal Works was founded in 1908 in downtown Minneapolis, Minnesota, and now operates from New Brighton. The company traces its roots to the region's booming commodity trade, where it designed custom dust-collection systems for grain elevators and mills.

Today the shop provides custom metal fabrication and machining, producing large and small components, assemblies, and structures. Its core processes include bending, forming, welding, and assembly of sheet, tube plate, round, bar, and angle stock. The facility works with stainless steel, brass, mild steel, galvanized metal, aluminum, and copper, and maintains unique dies for items such as street-light posts and spiral-chute flighting.

The company serves customers in paper manufacturing, industrial storage, agriculture, and environmental control. Documented projects include a custom safety guard for International Paper, stainless-steel hoppers for ferrite storage at Tundra Companies, discharge downspouts for an auto-glide conveyor at Dakota Growers, and a high-temperature heat exchanger for Environmental Control Solutions, Inc.

The firm emphasizes its 100-plus years of experience and a partnership approach, stating it is committed to delivering projects on time and to full customer satisfaction. Its founding mission — solving dust-collection challenges for the grain industry — remains a reference point for its problem-solving orientation.

Consumer and industrial clients order firearm components, personal protection device parts, musical instrument accessories, and footwear components. The company also supplies OEM-alternative laboratory plasticware such as digestion vessels, autosampler cups, viscometer vials, and titration beakers for elemental analysis instruments.

The company’s founding principle emphasizes getting the mold right, asserting that a correct mold minimizes the impact of molding process variability on part quality. MoldPro also highlights its “can do” moldmaking reputation, noting it has developed methods to produce parts other firms deemed impossible to injection mold.

about:
Morton Solar, LLC was founded in 2006 by Brad Morton in Evansville, Indiana. The firm operates as a full-service solar and electrical contractor, delivering engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) for residential, commercial, industrial, agricultural, and utility-scale photovoltaic systems. It also installs battery energy storage systems, including Tesla Powerwall and commercial BESS, EV charging infrastructure, and provides commercial and industrial electrical contracting through its parent company, Morton Electric, covering automation and controls, power distribution, panel building, and advanced manufacturing support. Notable installations include a 1.4 MW system for Vuteq in Princeton, a 2 MW array for AstraZeneca in Mount Vernon, and a 540 kW solar canopy for Orthopaedic Associates in Newburgh.

Morton Solar serves homeowners, businesses, farms, nonprofits, municipalities, schools, medical facilities, and industrial manufacturers across southern Indiana, western Kentucky, and southeastern Illinois. Its public-sector portfolio includes two of the nation's first net-zero energy public buildings—Richardsville Elementary School and Chrisney Library—as well as projects for utilities and government agencies.

The company distinguishes itself through a values-driven model, holding B Corp certification and membership in the Amicus Solar Cooperative. Its team includes NABCEP-certified professionals and an in-house grant writer for USDA REAP grants, and it is an approved SREC vendor for the Illinois Shines program. Morton Solar has also advocated for policy changes that expanded net-metering and streamlined interconnection processes in Indiana.

old_description: Founded in 2007 by Karen Hostetler, the mill was born from a mission to preserve the ranching culture of the Great American West. about:
Mountain Meadow Wool Mill was founded in 2007 by Karen Hostetler in Buffalo, Wyoming. The mill emerged from a mission to preserve the ranching culture of the Great American West, where Basque sheepherders had established small ranches in the late 1800s. Declining wool prices over the preceding decades threatened those operations, prompting Hostetler and her partner to open a full-service mill that would offer fair prices to ranchers for their wool.

The mill handles the entire wool supply chain under one roof: it sources fleece directly from Wyoming ranches, then scours, cards, spins, and knits the fiber into finished goods. Operations include custom processing for outside growers, in-house spinning of yarn, and knitting of apparel, blankets, and home goods. The facility also runs an eco-friendly processing line and maintains a retail shop and wholesale program.

Primary customers are Wyoming sheep ranchers who sell their clip to the mill, as well as wholesale buyers and direct consumers seeking American-made wool yarn, knitting kits, baby blankets, beanies, and wearable art. The mill has supplied fiber for University of Wyoming branded products and collaborates with local artisans through its Legacy Yarn Guild.

Hostetler started the business to reverse the decline of the region’s wool economy and to keep processing jobs in Wyoming. The company emphasizes traceability from ranch to home, fair pricing for producers, and environmentally responsible methods that preserve wool’s natural softness and durability.

name: MxD
old_description: MxD (Manufacturing x Digital), the nation’s Digital Manufacturing & Cybersecurity Institute, is a solution-neutral advisor and convener. In partnership with the U.S. Department of War, we work to strengthen the U.S. industrial base.
about:
MxD operates from Chicago, Illinois, where it was founded in 2014 as the Digital Manufacturing and Design Innovation Institute (DMDII). It is the second of 18 institutes in the Manufacturing USA network, a national initiative to secure the future of U.S. manufacturing through innovation, collaboration, and education. The institute was established in partnership with the U.S. Department of War, which remains a founding member and co-investor in its research and demonstration portfolio.

Members such as Siemens, EY, DMG MORI, and Betacom use the floor for experimentation with AI, robotics, AR/VR, digital twins, and 5G. MxD's three pillars — convene, advance, empower — guide its work: convening manufacturers, academia, and government; advancing digital adoption and secure cybersecurity practices; and empowering the workforce through accessible learning tools. More than 350,000 learners have engaged with MxD Learn programs, and the Virtual Training Center offers online courses from AI to cybersecurity.

MxD serves the U.S. industrial base with a focus on defense collaboration. As the Department of War-designated National Center for Cybersecurity in Manufacturing, it develops programs to protect supply chains from cyber attacks, including a Cyber Resource Hub and CMMC compliance guidance. The institute works closely with the Organic Industrial Base — government-owned facilities that produce munitions and maintain weapon systems — to modernize Army and Marine Corps industrial operations. Its network of over 350 members spans industry, academia, and government.

MxD was created to transform the outdated image of manufacturing into a clean, safe, and visionary technology leader, improving productivity, quality, and global competitiveness. Its mission is to strengthen U.S. manufacturing competitiveness through technology innovation, workforce development, and cybersecurity preparedness, ensuring a reliable industrial backstop in times of war and emergency.

National Content & Technology Cooperative (NCTC) is a not-for-profit cooperative headquartered in Overland Park, Kansas. Its founding mission was to help members competitively acquire video programming and vital technologies needed to offer services that define their communities’ infrastructure.

The cooperative negotiates programming and streaming agreements with more than 200 TV networks on behalf of its 700-plus member companies, which collectively serve roughly one-third of all households and businesses in North America and U.S. territories. Its connectivity portfolio includes IP transit and transport, DDoS mitigation, analytics, SD-WAN, DNS, cloud, and CDN services. NCTC also offers video platform solutions and operates a group-purchasing marketplace that gives members a single point of contact for technology procurement, contract management, and supplier performance.

The cooperative’s members are independent communications service providers—broadband and pay-TV operators—ranging from small rural operators to larger regional players. Network providers and suppliers such as CommScope, eero, TiVo, Cogent Communications, Lumen, and Zayo Group work through NCTC as a gateway to reach this diverse member base. NCTC’s supplier directory lists dozens of approved and preferred partners across hardware, software, and professional services.

NCTC’s differentiating premise is that collective purchasing power enables members to secure deals they could not obtain individually. The cooperative emphasizes a streamlined, one-stop procurement process, defined service-level commitments, and ongoing technology innovation to help members remain profitable and sustainable in a rapidly changing industry.

old_description: Never Stop Building is a design-build studio located in central Maine. We specialize in traditional woodworking, furniture design, timber framing, tokonoma, shoji doors, and gates, utilizing predominantly Japanese tools and techniques.
about:
The company was founded in 2013 by Jason Fox, who initially launched the venture as an engineering and prototyping business. A lifelong interest in Japanese history and culture, combined with a background in machining and computer-aided design, eventually steered the firm toward the precise world of Japanese woodworking.

The studio specializes in traditional woodworking, furniture design, timber framing, and finish carpentry, producing items such as tokonoma alcoves, shoji doors, gates, and custom furniture pieces. Work is carried out using predominantly Japanese hand tools and techniques, and the shop also passes on those methods through woodworking classes and timber-frame workshops often led by guest masters. Project examples include a yellow cedar partition wall, a fir slab dining island, a walnut entry door, and a hexagonal hot tub.

Past projects range from a garden shed and a mountain home to a Kyoto-inspired tea room, a sushi counter, and a sauna, indicating a focus on high-quality, bespoke installations for both private and public environments.

Fox describes the company's guiding principle as a covenant to "honor the tree," sourcing lumber directly when possible and favoring natural finishes. The design philosophy blends Japanese aesthetics with Shaker and Mid-Century Modern influences, aiming for what he calls "utilitarian elegance" — simple, clean forms that let the material speak for itself.

New England Truck Design operates from Sterling, Massachusetts, where it was founded in 1977 by Kevin Lavin after his tenure at Wolf Coach building custom emergency vehicles.

The company designs and builds custom aluminum and stainless-steel truck bodies including dump, grain/chipper, flatbed, switch‑n‑go, fire apparatus, and specialty bodies for trucks ranging from pickups to 10‑wheelers. Lavin’s team emphasizes longevity over weight savings, using extruded structural sills instead of formed members and a proprietary linear cam latch that removes bell‑crank linkages, allowing higher toolbox mounting. In‑house electrical work and a policy of overbuilding for the work environment are cited as core differentiators.

old_description: Our small veteran owned artisanal sea salt company follows the traditional and unhurried process of crafting small batches of 100% pure and natural sea salt. Nothing added, nothing taken away. Our local Sea salt contains no anti-caking, bleaching or iodine additives. However, it does retain numerous trace minerals such as Calcium, Magnesium and Potassium. about:
Newport Sea Salt Co. operates from Newport, Rhode Island, where husband-and-wife team Matt and Tami Mullins founded the business after Matt’s 20-year career as a U.S. Naval Officer. The veteran-owned, woman-owned small business began with a desire to stay connected to the sea and to produce artisanal sea salt using traditional hand-harvesting methods.

The company hand-harvests seawater from Brenton Reef at high tide, filters it, and evaporates it in small batches to produce 100% natural flake sea salt with no additives. The product line includes plain flake salt and blended varieties such as Rosemary & Thyme, Butcher’s Blend, Bella Napoli, and Fire Salt. Production is small-scale, with the Mullins family and their sons Matthew and Connor comprising the crew.

Newport Sea Salt Co. sells directly to consumers at farmers markets and pop-up events across Rhode Island, and through retail partners including specialty food shops, cheese purveyors, and seafood markets in Rhode Island, New York, and California. The salt is also used by restaurant chefs and home cooks as a finishing salt.

The founders emphasize their unhurried, traditional process and the purity of their source water—an approved shellfish-growing area monitored by the Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management. They highlight that their salt retains trace minerals such as calcium, magnesium, and potassium, and contains no anti-caking agents, bleach, or iodine.

about:
Nextern is headquartered in Maple Grove, Minnesota. Founded in the early 2000s as an engineering and manufacturing partner for industrial components, the company shifted its focus to medical device electromechanical systems in 2016. In 2022, it acquired NPX Precision Technologies, adding nitinol and specialty alloy expertise, and consolidated product development into its new Maple Grove headquarters in 2024.

The company provides vertically integrated medical device development and manufacturing across four pillars: product development, manufacturing, precision technologies (NPX), and consulting services. Its capabilities span design-for-manufacturability, phase-gate development, agile sprints, nitinol shape-setting, laser cutting and welding (±0.0005″ tolerance), catheter shaft assembly, braiding, coiling, tip forming, and regulatory, clinical, and quality consulting. Operations run across five global sites: Maple Grove (HQ, development, manufacturing), Cartago, Costa Rica (manufacturing), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam (manufacturing), Kenosha, Wisconsin (precision components), and Shenzhen, China (strategic sourcing).

Nextern serves OEMs, clinicians, and innovators in the medical device sector, with deep clinical market expertise in peripheral vascular (specialty wires, thrombectomy systems, renal denervation), interventional cardiology (delivery catheters, IVL catheters, balloon catheters), neuromodulation (pulse generators, implantable leads, wearable neurostim), electrophysiology (PFA generators, RF generators, ablation catheters), and structural heart (transcatheter delivery, implant frames, occlusion devices).

The company’s stated mission is to partner across the entire product lifecycle to solve patient needs and improve lives. Its differentiation rests on a vertically integrated model that embeds manufacturability from day one, a BioSimulation Lab for realistic device testing, and a phase-gate process designed to eliminate uncertainty early. The 2026 launch of consulting services extends its reach into regulatory strategy, clinical evidence, quality systems, and lifecycle management.

about:
The New Jersey Cable and Internet Association (NJCIA) is headquartered in Trenton, New Jersey. Founded in 1965 as a voluntary trade organization, it serves as the collective voice for the state's major cable telecommunications providers. The association operates under a board of directors drawn from its member companies.

NJCIA does not manufacture products; rather, it provides industry representation, government affairs advocacy, and economic research on behalf of its members—Comcast Cable Communications, Altice USA (operator of the Optimum brand), and Charter Communications (operator of the Spectrum brand). The association reports that its members collectively contribute $12.6 billion in economic impact to New Jersey and sustain approximately 75,975 direct and indirect jobs across all 12 congressional districts. Activities include advocating for broadband infrastructure investment, supporting federal programs such as the Affordable Connectivity Program, and publishing industry data.

The association serves the cable telecommunications, broadband internet, video services, and mobile communications industries in New Jersey. Its work benefits residents and businesses statewide by promoting network expansion and connectivity. As a state chapter affiliated with the National Cable & Telecommunications Association (NCTA), NJCIA coordinates with national policy efforts.

The organization was established to unify the cable industry's voice in Trenton and to demonstrate the sector's economic value to policymakers and the public. Member companies state that continued infrastructure investment is essential to meeting growing demand for high-quality broadband, video, and mobile services.

old_description: Norwood Medical began in 1926 as a tool and die shop. The company worked on tooling for its first medical application in the 1970s. about:
Norwood Medical operates from a 700,000-square-foot manufacturing campus in Dayton, Ohio. The company traces its roots to 1926 when it began as a tool and die shop. A local businessman who had worked at the firm since 1950 purchased the business with a partner in 1981, and by the 1990s the operation had evolved into component manufacturing. Medical component manufacturing and assembly became its sole focus in the early 2000s. In 2021, Norwood was acquired by the Heraeus Group, a family-owned German technology group, preserving its family-oriented culture.

The company provides end-to-end contract manufacturing for medical devices, offering more than 30 in-house engineering and production capabilities. Core processes include CNC milling and turning (horizontal, vertical, and 5-axis), CNC Swiss machining, metal injection molding (MIM) with in-house feedstock formulation, insert injection molding, electrical discharge machining (wire and RAM), electrochemical machining (ECM), precision metal stamping, and water-jet cutting. Value-added post-processing covers laser marking and welding, polishing, electropolishing, heat treating, coating (PTFE dry film, sodium stearate, siliconization), ultrasonic cleaning, overmolding, and passivation. Testing, assembly, and packaging are performed in controlled environments supported by nine on-site quality labs. The campus houses over 800 CNC machines and supports production volumes from prototype to full-scale runs, with products used in more than 13 million surgeries annually.

Norwood serves the medical device industry, focusing on cardiovascular, minimally invasive surgery (MIS), orthopedics, robotic-assisted surgery (RAS), and surgical technologies. Its customers include well-known medical device OEMs that rely on the company for complex robotic instruments, energy-sealing devices, and other critical components.

The company emphasizes its vertically integrated model, long-term ownership perspective, and quality mindset as differentiators. It reinvests 3% of revenue annually in automation, maintains a 95% customer retention rate, and operates nine in-house metrology labs equipped with CMM, CT scanning, optical inspection, and laser scanning systems. A dedicated regulatory and compliance department ensures adherence to ISO 13485:2016, FDA 21 CFR 820, and ISO 14971:2019 standards.

name: Outokumpu
old_description: Americas most technically advanced stainless steel mill, Outokumpu Calvert offers a comprehensive product portfolio combined with industry-leading technical support and services. The mill is now adding ferritic grades to its already well-established portfolio, perfectly suited to American manufacturing. Download the ferritic stainless steels datasheet below.
about:
Outokumpu Calvert operates a fully integrated stainless steel mill in Calvert, Alabama. The facility is owned by Outokumpu Stainless USA, LLC, a subsidiary of the global Outokumpu group. While the mill draws on more than a century of stainless steel expertise dating to the invention of the material, the Calvert site itself was developed as a state-of-the-art production hub for the Americas market.

The mill performs all primary steelmaking steps on site – melting, casting, hot rolling, annealing and pickling, and cold rolling – along with finishing lines that provide polishing, slitting, and cut-to-length services. It produces hot‑rolled and cold‑rolled coil, strip, sheet, and plate across four product families: Moda (ferritic grades for mildly corrosive environments), Core (austenitic and ferritic grades for medium corrosion), Supra (grades for highly corrosive environments), and Forta (high‑strength grades enabling weight reduction). A coil service center network supports tailored finishing and logistics.

The mill serves automotive and transportation (exhaust systems, chassis components, decorative trim), chemical and petrochemical processing (sour‑gas components, high‑temperature equipment), food and beverage, tank manufacturing, infrastructure (bridge structures, floodgates, rebar), machine building, energy, pulp and paper, and tube manufacturing. Specific applications include rocket engine parts, sugar‑industry equipment, sinks and deep‑drawn products, and structural components for bridges.

Outokumpu positions Calvert as the most technically advanced stainless steel mill in the Americas, emphasizing its fully integrated flow, progressive steelmaking technology, and industry‑technical support. The addition of ferritic grades expands the portfolio for U.S. manufacturing, and the facility’s operational excellence was recognized with a 2018 Steel Excellence Award from American Metal Market.

HTI Plastics runs a facility with 24 Krauss Maffei injection molding machines ranging from 55 to 1,800 tons, while Lincoln Plastics specializes in plastic extrusion profiles. All three manufacturing sites are ISO 9001 registered, and HTI Plastics holds FDA approval and ISO 13485 certification.

The company serves agriculture, food, pharmaceutical, sporting goods, animal health, and food packaging markets. Its pharmaceutical applicators are used in both prescription and over-the-counter treatments, and it produces custom thermoplastic injection-molded components for a variety of proprietary and custom applications.

PCE emphasizes growth through acquisition and complementary product development, continuous investment in the latest plastics manufacturing technology, and employee training backed by modern facilities and equipment to maximize quality output.

The facility processes roughly 27 million bushels of corn annually to produce 86 million gallons of bioethanol, along with a suite of co-products including dried distillers grains, wet distillers grains, distillers corn oil, condensed distillers solubles (syrup), and pelletized feed products.

Primary markets include fuel blenders for bioethanol, livestock and poultry feed manufacturers for distillers grains and corn oil, and industrial users such as biodiesel producers, ink and paint formulators. POET emphasizes an integrated business model that combines research and development with design, construction, technology, operations, public affairs, and marketing. Operating from a single facility at 254 36th Street, the company functions as a design studio and full-service sample factory. Its in-house team handles pattern making, sample making, fabric and trim sourcing, cut-and-sew production, grading, fitting, and draping. The factory focuses on low-minimum-order production for emerging and sustainable brands, while also developing footwear lines through established manufacturing relationships in Europe, Asia, and South America.

Panah Project serves a range of clients including established apparel brands, emerging designers, startups, film and theater productions, footwear labels, and bespoke clients seeking one-of-a-kind pieces such as red-carpet looks. For film and theater, the studio creates bespoke costumes tailored to actor measurements and production timelines; for footwear, it supports development across all major categories with flexible minimums.

The founders cite their Nairobi experience as the foundation for the studio's values—fair wages, long-term opportunity, and craftsmanship. Morteza Saifi, formerly Executive Creative Director at Camuto Group, leads creative and technical direction, while Evgeniya Khromina guides strategy and operations. The company emphasizes a streamlined, under-one-roof process that maintains quality control from design through to market-ready pieces.

name: Par Hawaii Refining
old_description: We have deep roots in the islands. We started as The Gas Company in 1904, and as a way to provide more energy security for the islands, built a refinery in Campbell Industrial Park in Kapolei. With the support of local government officials and Hawaii’s congressional delegation, Hawaii was able to establish a refinery, which has been in operation in a Foreign-Trade Zone since 1972. Pacific Resources, Inc. (PRI) became the holding company of The Gas Company and the refinery.
about:
Par Hawaii Refining traces its roots to 1904 when The Gas Company was established in Hawaii. Pacific Resources, Inc. (PRI) became the holding company for both the gas utility and the refinery. Today, Par Hawaii is a subsidiary of Par Pacific Holdings (NYSE: PARR), headquartered in Houston, Texas, while its corporate offices remain in Kapolei on Oahu.

The company operates the only petroleum refinery in Hawaii, where 660 employees run 24/7 operations to convert imported crude oil into gasoline, diesel, fuel oil, ship fuel, and aviation fuels including jet fuel. Refined products move through an integrated logistics network of pipelines, tanker trucks, and barges serving all major Hawaiian islands. Par Hawaii also markets fuels through a statewide retail network of Hele, 76, and nomnom-branded stations. The refinery supplies the energy needs of roughly 1.4 million residents and 8 million annual visitors.

Primary customers include electric and gas utilities, major airlines such as Hawaiian Airlines and Alaska Airlines, the U.S. military, and the general public via retail outlets. Par Hawaii has also formed a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corp. and ENEOS Corp. to develop renewable fuels, and is collaborating with Hawaiian Airlines to explore sustainable aviation fuel production by retooling an existing refinery unit.

The company states its mission as "Humbly Serving Communities," emphasizing reliable, safe, and environmentally responsible energy supply for an isolated island state. Leadership cites integrity, creativity, hard work, and respect as core values guiding a transition toward decarbonization, including carbon sequestration and renewable fuel production, to meet Hawaii's ambitious clean-energy goals.

Phase Sensitive Innovations (PSI) is a small, high-technology company based in Newark, Delaware, specializing in RF photonic devices, components, and systems with a focus on the millimeter-wave region of the electromagnetic spectrum.

The company designs and manufactures high-speed UTC photodiodes, ultra-high-speed lithium niobate phase modulators (up to 500 GHz), broadband RF photonic links, and tunable optical paired source (TOPS) systems for wideband RF signal synthesis. It provides a full suite of photonic integrated circuit (PIC) capabilities — design, simulation, layout, multi-project wafer submission, and characterization — alongside custom RF design, RF component testing from DC to 1 THz, and RF/optical packaging (flip-chip, wire/ribbon bonding, hermetic sealing). The shop also runs a Mazak V500C CNC mill (3-axis and 3D simultaneous) and a 3NTR A2V4 3D printer for multi-material polymer parts.

Its devices enable millimeter-wave imaging for security scanning and vision enhancement, RF-over-fiber links, antenna remoting, phased-array beamforming, and RF surveillance across microwave, millimeter-wave, and terahertz bands.

The company emphasizes its phase-locking upconversion technology, which it says delivers unprecedented beam-bandwidth processing for next-generation 5G and beyond. It also highlights photodiode power handling and linearity, lithium niobate modulators covering the full millimeter-wave spectrum, and an end-to-end PIC design-to-fabrication flow under an ISO 9001:2015 quality system certified by TÜV SÜD.

old_description: Since 1946, Pioneer Automotive Industries has been dedicated to delivering high-quality automotive components with precision and reliability. Our commitment to innovation, engineering excellence, and customer satisfaction has made us a trusted partner across the Americas.
about:
Pioneer Automotive Industries was founded in 1946 by Herman A. Shields in Meridian, Mississippi. The company began as a manufacturer of engine and transmission components. Over the decades it changed hands several times: acquired by The Barnes Group in 1979, then by UIS Inc. in 1993, then by United Components (part of The Carlyle Group) in 2003, then ownership transitioned to Doron Arad in 2006, and later joined The Lodi Group in 2009–2010. In 2017 it acquired ATP Automotive and expanded its Meridian facility to 300,000 square feet in 2018.

Today Pioneer operates a 300,000 sq ft manufacturing and distribution facility in Meridian, producing over 15,000 SKUs of powertrain and transmission components. Its product lines include flexplates, flywheels, automatic and manual transmission shift cables, clutch cables, speedometer cables, engine mounts, harmonic balancers, and a range of high‑performance parts. The company designs, manufactures, and distributes these components for the automotive aftermarket.

Pioneer serves customers and distributors throughout the United States, Canada, and Latin America.

PDM serves a diverse industrial base including automotive, electronics, medical, industrial equipment, sporting goods and firearms, pet products, agricultural, construction, consumer goods, and battery components.

The company emphasizes low-overhead, non-union facilities operating 24 hours a day, five to seven days a week, with global sourcing capabilities. about:
Plastic Design Company (PDC) is based in Scottsdale, Arizona, where it operates a vertically integrated facility specializing in precision injection molding and micro-molding for medical device, diagnostics, and biotechnology applications. The company partners with OEMs and contract manufacturers worldwide.

PDC provides precision injection molding, micro-molding, insert molding, and over-molding services, supported by in-house tool design and mold fabrication. All production takes place in an ISO 8 cleanroom equipped with automated machinery. The company works with high-performance thermoplastics such as PEEK, COC, COP, PEBA, polycarbonate, PMMA, and polystyrene, and can customize material blends with colorants and functional additives. Its capabilities span from design and development through high-volume production, including value-added assembly, measurement, inspection, and program management.

The company serves medical device OEMs and contract manufacturers across segments including diagnostics, drug delivery, orthopedic sports medicine, proteomics and genomics, robotic assisted surgery, and vascular surgery. Typical components produced include multi-part diagnostic cartridge housings with molded-in alignment features, surgical instrument assemblies with rod-based actuation components, implantable or wearable components with over-molded metal contacts, capillary components, lateral flow assay components, optical components, valve components, and cannula assemblies.

PDC emphasizes its vertically integrated model, noting that in-house tooling gives it control over iterations and scheduling, while its cleanroom environment and material expertise enable quick decision-making and flexibility for complex medical applications.

name: Plastipak Packaging Inc
old_description: One of those innovations was the creation of Plastipak—founded in 1967 to solve the problem of the heavy five-gallon jugs used to deliver water. With a full load of water in them, these five-gallon jugs weighed 50 pounds and required superior strength to manage. Plastic seemed the ideal solution to lighten the load, as did manufacturing the plastic in-house. The success of the lightened bottle was the start of Plastipak’s ongoing innovation and success.
about:
Plastipak Packaging Inc. was founded in 1967 in Champaign, Illinois, by Bill Young, who joined his family's water delivery business after graduating from the University of Detroit.

Today Plastipak operates as a global manufacturer of rigid plastic packaging and recycling solutions, with more than 50 production sites across North America, South America, Europe, Africa, and Asia. Its core processes include extrusion blow molding, injection stretch blow molding (ISBM), PET and ePET molding, wide-mouth container technology, hot-fill and barrier container engineering, decoration (embossing, debossing, direct-object printing), and the production of both virgin and post-consumer recycled (PCR) resins. The company holds over 500 U.S. patents and more than 1,000 international patents, reflecting a portfolio of proprietary systems such as the rotary dual-cavity ISBM machine, the 30-station G.E.M. PAK extrusion wheel, and recent innovations like SprayPET Revolution™ aerosol packaging, PPK Natura™ carbon-waste PET resin, and O2blox™ nylon-free oxygen barrier.

Plastipak serves a broad range of end markets, including carbonated and non-carbonated beverages, hot-fill juices and teas, beer, UHT milk, dairy, household and commercial products (detergents, personal care), automotive, industrial, and agricultural chemicals. Long-standing customers have included Pepsi, Kraft, Heineken, Downy Unstopables, and Hilltop Honey, illustrating the company's reach across multinational brands and regional producers alike.

Plastipak differentiates itself through vertical integration (in-house resin production, mold design, recycling via its Clean Tech centers), a global footprint that enables local service, and a sustained investment in circular-economy technologies that turn post-consumer waste into new packaging.

about:
Podiumwear Custom Sports Apparel was founded in 2003 in St. Paul, Minnesota, by Reid Lutter, a nordic ski racer and coach with four decades of trail experience. Frustrated by the difficulties of ordering custom uniforms for his own teams, Lutter set out to build a company that would make the process enjoyable and stress‑free, starting with nordic ski apparel before expanding into cycling, running, and soccer.

The company produces fully custom team uniforms and apparel — jerseys, tops, shorts, training jackets, pants, and socks — for a wide range of sports including cycling, nordic skiing, running, soccer, volleyball, football, basketball, hockey, lacrosse, clay target sports, softball, baseball, mountain biking, cross‑country, and track and field. Customers work one‑on‑one with designers or use an online customizer, and orders can be shipped directly to each athlete or to a single team contact. A partnership with The North Face and U.S. Ski & Snowboard adds a high‑profile dimension to its nordic program.

Podiumwear serves youth, club, and school teams across the United States and internationally. Its customers include team uniform directors, coaches, administrators, and parents who need reliable, on‑time delivery for seasonal competition. The company highlights testimonials from a team uniform director, a team administrator, and a club parent, underscoring its focus on easing the administrative burden of uniform procurement.

Lutter’s original goal — concierge‑level service, fast turnaround, and top‑tier quality — remains the stated differentiator. Podiumwear emphasizes total design freedom without templates, durability that lasts multiple seasons, and a policy that allows two below‑minimum re‑orders per calendar year to accommodate roster changes.

Point Medical Corporation operates from Crown Point, Indiana, where it develops and fabricates implant-grade silicone rubber devices and assemblies for medical applications. The company focuses on custom development and fabrication to meet exacting tolerances and specifications required in the medical environment.

The facility is FDA-registered and ISO 13485:2016 certified, with a Class 10,000 clean room. In-house prototype development and tooling accelerate the transition to production. Capabilities span extrusion (custom, multi-lumen, co-extrusion, miniature profiles, wire-reinforced, striped, close-tolerance, translucent, radiopaque), catheter assembly (smooth transition tube-to-lumen molding, balloons, coil forming, printing, complete fabrication, latex-to-silicone conversion), molding (liquid injection, top transfer, compression, insert), and tipping (forming, clean-cut holes, step cutting, taper and bullet tips).

Point Medical serves medical device manufacturers and clinical consultants, providing custom silicone rubber components for applications such as catheters, tubing, and implantable assemblies. The company also operates Martech Medical Products for non-silicone plastics manufacturing.

The company emphasizes an ongoing inquiry into the latest technology, materials, and manufacturing methods to ensure custom product performance. Its reputation for quality and innovative design stems from consistent attention to materials, machining, and manufacturing techniques.

old_description: Founded in Harborcreek, Pennsylvania, in 1953, Port Erie Plastics remains family-owned and engineering-driven. We combine the responsiveness of a privately held manufacturer with the infrastructure of a large-scale production partner.
about:
Port Erie Plastics was founded in 1953 in Harborcreek, Pennsylvania, and remains a family-owned, engineering-driven manufacturer.

The company specializes in custom plastic injection molding and structural foam injection molding for large components, with wall thicknesses from 0.200 to 0.500 inches and part lengths up to 7.5 feet. Its facility runs nearly 90 injection molding machines in a 24/7 production environment, supported by a full-service in-house tool room that handles mold building, refurbishment, and maintenance. Port Erie also manages structured tool transfers and validation, often bringing transferred molds into steady production within days.

Port Erie serves OEMs across consumer products, office furniture, durable goods, building materials, home improvement, kitchen and appliance components, electronic housings, material handling, lawn and garden, and building and construction. Past programs include structural foam redesign of HDPE trench drains for the construction industry, injection molding of polypropylene and elastomer lids for cookware, and development of combination dials for safe manufacturing. The company also supported an urgent medical product mold transfer that restored production in a single weekend.

The company says its differentiation lies in disciplined tooling control, process validation, and a project engineer assigned to each program for technical ownership from quote through full production. Its core values—Protect, Engage, Perform—guide a focus on long-term partnerships, supply continuity, and protection of customer tooling investments.

Based in Reading, Pennsylvania, Poward Plastics has been producing custom plastic injection molded parts for over 50 years. The company is family-owned and operated across multiple generations, with materials sourced from U.S. suppliers and all manufacturing completed domestically.

The shop runs injection molding presses from 25 to 120 tons in-house and partners with facilities up to 6,000 tons, with a maximum press size of 1,400 tons. Services include insert molding, overmolding, prototype and production tooling (aluminum and P20 steel), multi-cavity and family molds, mold building, repair, and maintenance, as well as 3D printing and CNC modeling for prototyping. Minimum orders start at 100 parts with a $5,000 threshold.

Customers span medical (valves, syringes, bushings), automotive (plugs, fittings), electronics (housings, accessories), aerospace and defense (ITAR-registered), food and beverage, packaging and displays, industrial, and government sectors. The company ships nationwide and offers free local delivery in the Reading area.

Poward Plastics emphasizes domestic sourcing and production, mold storage and warehousing for reorders, and experience transferring tooling from offshore manufacturers. It holds ITAR and RoHS certifications and provides design engineering assistance, rapid tooling in two weeks, and production tooling in three weeks.

about:
Power Plus is headquartered in Anaheim, California, and was founded in 1987 by Steve Bray. Bray, a former electrician working on Southern California construction sites, recognized that contractors needed more than equipment—they needed reliable problem-solvers. The company began as a small temporary power operation in Orange County.

Today, Power Plus operates nationwide with 500–999 employees and describes itself as the largest independent power solutions provider in America. Services span utility infrastructure, permanent electrical installation, and portable equipment sales.

The company serves construction, oil and gas, mining, disaster response, agriculture, healthcare, data centers, retail distribution, commercial facilities, critical infrastructure, and telecommunications. Its customer base includes Amazon, Walmart, Costco, and roughly half of the Fortune 100. In the 1990s, Power Plus supplied power for global entertainment productions such as the Rolling Stones tour, Olympic events, and the Super Bowl.

Power Plus emphasizes a problem-solving culture: technicians walk sites, listen to requirements, and design custom solutions rather than offering cookie-cutter packages. The firm maintained a no-layoff policy during the COVID-19 pandemic, reflecting a people-first philosophy rooted in Bray’s original vision of doing whatever it takes to deliver power whenever and wherever it is needed.

about:
Precise Connections, Inc. has operated from Duncanville, Texas, since 1985.

The company provides end-to-end electronics manufacturing services, including PCB assembly (through-hole, surface-mount, and mixed-technology), custom box builds, cable and wire harness assembly, design-for-manufacturing consultation, functional testing, and supply-chain management. Prototypes and full production runs share the same floor, supported by an Aptean Made2Manage ERP system with Panasonic PanaCIM lot traceability and RFID-tracked inventory. The facility maintains a fully ESD-controlled environment with calibrated test equipment and a formal corrective-action process.

Precise serves OEMs across regulated and performance-critical markets such as energy storage, medical devices, industrial equipment, printing, audio, marine and marine audio, safety devices, railway, control systems, motion detection, IT and networking, and consumer products. The company also supports OEM programs and aftermarket service. Components are sourced globally through authorized distributors and factory-direct channels, with broker assistance for hard-to-find parts.

The firm emphasizes a single-point-of-contact model from design handoff through fulfillment, describing itself as "big enough to deliver, small enough to be agile." Its quality system is certified to ISO 9001:2015 and compliant with IPC-A-610 and IPC/WHMA-A-620 up to Class III, with RoHS 2 adherence across all processes. In 2025, customer ratings earned Precise the Circuits Assembly Service Excellence Award for Responsiveness among EMS providers under $20 million in sales. The company cites 30 consecutive profitable quarters and a staff averaging more than ten years of industry experience as indicators of stability.

Precision Medical Technologies operates three facilities in northern Indiana, headquartered in Warsaw. The company has held ISO 13485:2016 certification since 2003 through SGS United Kingdom Limited, though its founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The company provides end-to-end contract manufacturing for orthopedic implants, components, and instrumentation. Its capabilities span design for manufacturability, prototyping, and high-volume production using precision CNC machining, Swiss turning, casting, turning, and finishing. All production is documented through device history records, with in-process inspections, final inspection, and product release audits. Sterile packaging and supply chain management complete the in-house offering.

Precision Medical Technologies serves original equipment manufacturers in orthopedics, including knee, hip, spine, shoulder, trauma and extremities, and minimally invasive surgery markets. Customers rely on the firm for tibial trays, femoral components, patellar components, and partial or total knee implants and instrumentation.

The company emphasizes a 24-hour quote response, vertical integration across its three Indiana sites, and the ability to complete production in a single operation. Its quality system maintains IQ, OQ, and PQ validation, with dimensional accuracy monitored via CMMs, optical comparators, and Keyence measuring systems.

The company emphasizes a one‑roof model that combines tooling, molding, finishing, and logistics, offers reshoring assistance and mold‑transfer services, and maintains an environmental focus that recycles materials and generates less non‑recyclable waste per week than the average household.

Precision Plastics, Inc. was founded in 1976 in Beltsville, Maryland, by its current owner with the goal of providing custom plastic fabrication services to a broad range of industries. Today the firm operates as a full-service plastics manufacturer offering design, engineering, and manufacturing under one roof. Its capabilities span concept development, industrial design, 3D modeling, prototyping, testing, production planning, material sourcing, and finishing services such as engraving, polishing, and assembly. Fabrications range from one-of-a-kind prototypes to short-run production in plastics, wood, laminate, and metals.

The customer base includes retail chains, the U.S. Navy (for quarter-scale rocket models), national museums requiring complex display cases and archival enclosures, scientific and microscopy facilities needing precision instrument housings, trade-show exhibitors, signage and wayfinding programs, and makers of acrylic furniture and podiums. Projects have included museum-quality cases, laboratory equipment enclosures, trade-show displays, custom podiums, and interior signage systems.

Precision Plastics attributes its differentiation to nearly 50 years of industry experience, deep material expertise, innovative technology such as 3D design and digital fabrication integration, highly skilled craftspeople, rigorous quality control, and project management that keeps jobs on time and on budget.

Progressive Scale & Software Solutions was founded in 1976 in Bethel, Connecticut, at the moment the weighing industry was shifting from mechanical to electronic instruments.

Today the firm operates as a single-source integrator: it specifies Rice Lake, A&D, Digi, Ohaus, and Totalcomp indicators and platforms; programs PLC logic, label formats, and ERP connections; and fields factory-trained technicians for on-site calibration and repair across Connecticut and the Northeast. Its proprietary Windows-based Provision Processing System (PPS) serves meat, poultry, and seafood plants with catch-weight labeling, lot traceability, and QuickBooks integration. The customer base spans discrete manufacturing and protein processing. In manufacturing, the company delivers component counting and kitting, automated fill-to-target, checkweighing with barcode validation, and data collection to ERP, MES, and AS/400 systems. In meat, poultry, and seafood, it provides harvest stations, scale carts, washdown enclosures, and the PPS software for yield tracking and order fulfillment. Named references include PepsiCo, Stanley Black & Decker, Thule, Snake River Farms, United States Surgical (Covidien), a major switch manufacturer, and a fish processor using pay-by-weight stations.

The company says its differentiation lies in eliminating the vendor gap — it sells the scale, writes the controls and data-collection software, and calibrates the installed system, so responsibility for the integration rests with one team. Round-the-clock technician consultation is offered because a stopped line does not wait for business hours.

The customer base spans original equipment manufacturers, hospitals, clinics, and a global network of dealers and distributors. RadScan partners with OEMs to co‑design new imaging accessories and also sells its branded covers and pads directly to healthcare facilities worldwide.

The company emphasizes its regulatory expertise — maintaining ISO 13485, FDA, EU MDR, RoHS, and REACH compliance — and its American‑made manufacturing as key differentiators. old_description: We have been in business since 2012 with over 50 years of combined experience on staff. Our production space is located in Duxbury, Vermont, 5 minutes outside of Waterbury, just off of Route 100. about:
Real Tree Woodworking operates from a 3,500-square-foot shop in Duxbury, Vermont, just off Route 100 near Waterbury. The business traces its roots to 2004 when Jon Deerfield founded Nature's Curve Woodworking in an artist community in Niagara Falls, New York, after earning a BFA in Furniture Design and apprenticing with two master craftsmen—including work on a Frank Lloyd Wright house restoration. Deerfield relocated to Vermont in 2007 to join Wall/Goldfinger, a high-end commercial furniture maker serving clients such as the New York Stock Exchange, the White House, and the Federal Reserve. In spring 2012 he relaunched the venture as Real Tree Woodworking, which has grown steadily since.

The shop produces custom cabinetry, furniture, doors, and architectural trim on a build-to-order basis, and also offers piecework processing of solid wood, sheet goods, real wood veneer, and laminate for other builders and DIYers. A dedicated finishing room rounds out the in-house capabilities. The current team comprises Deerfield and three woodworkers—Matt Joyce (since 2022), John Crowne (since 2021), and D.J. Rummell (since 2025)—working in the 3,500 sq ft facility.

Customers span residential and commercial construction across Vermont and the East Coast (New Hampshire, Massachusetts, New York). The client base includes architects, designers, general contractors, and other woodworking shops. Notable past projects include commercial office furniture for Wall/Goldfinger's institutional accounts and the Frank Lloyd Wright restoration.

Deerfield emphasizes a "build it well and build it to last" philosophy rooted in his apprenticeship background and the disciplined production standards honed at Wall/Goldfinger, positioning the shop as a reliable partner for both one-off custom pieces and repeat production runs.

name: Riverland Industries, Inc.
old_description: Since opening in 1999 as a manufacturer of dry ATH, our story has been one of constant expansion and evolution. We’ve been growing for over 25 years — and every year marks an exciting new development in our capabilities. Here are just some of the highlights.
about:
Riverland Industries, Inc. opened in 1999 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, as a manufacturer of dry aluminum trihydrate (ATH). The company has expanded steadily over more than 25 years, evolving from a single-product operation into a full-service toll manufacturer.

Today Riverland operates as an industrial toll manufacturer, offering custom material processing across a range of unit operations. Its capabilities include size reduction, size separation, heat treating, impregnation, forming, blending, extrusion, particle size reduction, flash calcination, and granulation. Key equipment includes an indirect rotary kiln capable of product temperatures up to 815 °C and air classifiers for fine particle separation. An in-house laboratory provides moisture analysis, particle size distribution, surface area measurement, and porosimetry. The facility also provides warehousing, packaging, and freight management, with direct access to river, rail, and interstate transportation corridors. Headcount is listed as two employees in public records.

The company serves customers in petrochemical, chemical, food-grade, air purification, and water treatment markets. It specializes in adsorbent materials and has produced spherical alumina for a global producer. Partners typically engage Riverland for collaborative process engineering, flexible capital investment, and the design and deployment of dedicated equipment and facilities.

Riverland emphasizes scalable infrastructure and a flexible capital investment model that allows partner-driven expansion.

about:
Rivers Metal Products was founded in 1973 in Lincoln, Nebraska. The company began as a metal fabrication shop and has since expanded into rotational mold manufacturing and metal distribution.

The company provides custom metal fabrication, rotational mold tooling and repair, contract manufacturing, architectural and interior metalwork, signage, and fine art fabrication. Its shop is equipped for MIG, TIG, arc, and resistance welding; laser, plasma, and flame cutting; shearing, sawing, plate rolling, tube bending, pipe coiling, brake pressing, lathe and mill machining. Rivers Metal also stocks and distributes steel, stainless steel, aluminum, galvanized, polished, brushed, and hot- and cold-rolled sheet metal.

Rivers Metal serves industrial, architectural, artistic, and agricultural clients. Longtime partner Peregrine, Inc. has collaborated for more than 30 years. The firm has fabricated 22,000-gallon rotational molds, agricultural tanks, machinery components, stairways, railings, and public art installations such as the “Backyard Oasis” project for Loeck Designs and community pride sculptures.

The company says its differentiator lies in its consultative approach—guiding customers from material selection through design and production—and its half-century of experience pioneering fabricated stainless-steel rotational molds. Its mission emphasizes hard work, integrity, and customer service, aiming to improve quality of life for customers, employees, suppliers, and the community.
